finding.claim: Missing authorization on tenant wipe. wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws, and discards the result. Any authenticated user can run the destructive wipe without the OWNER role.
finding.source: Any authenticated caller of POST /tenants/{t}/wipe, with an arbitrary User and no OWNER role, and an attacker-chosen tenant path parameter.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 (destructive deletion of tenant data).

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is the handler for POST /tenants/{t}/wipe
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role), as its Javadoc says. It does not throw.
The boolean return value is ignored, so a user without OWNER passes through

finding.guards_checked: The only guard on the path is the requireRole call at line 26, which has no effect because its result is discarded. The sibling export() uses checkRole(), which throws, so it is correctly guarded. No other authentication, authorization or tenant-ownership check exists in the file.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole at src/Admin.java:14-16 returns a boolean and does not throw. Its result is discarded at line 26. The throwing checkRole (18-22) is used only in export(). No other guard exists.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls the non-throwing requireRole (14-16) as a bare statement, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any authenticated user without the OWNER role.

finding.claim: Role checks are not scoped to the tenant. Roles are global strings on User, and the tenant argument is never compared to the user's membership. An OWNER of any tenant, or any user holding a global OWNER role, can export or wipe another tenant's data (cross-tenant IDOR). This depends on how roles are assigned outside this file, so it is lower confidence.
finding.source: Authenticated user with OWNER role for their own tenant, supplying a different victim tenant id in the {t} path parameter.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33, and repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27.

trace.note: User holds only a name and a global set of roles, with no tenant association
checkRole(u, "OWNER") validates the role only, not ownership of the tenant
repo.export(tenant) runs with the attacker-supplied tenant id

finding.guards_checked: checkRole confirms the OWNER role only. No comparison between the user and the tenant exists in this file. Any tenant scoping in the Repo implementation or an upstream layer was not available to inspect.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole at src/Admin.java:18-22 (throws SecurityException, role-only, correctly used at line 32); requireRole at line 14 returns a boolean that is discarded at line 26. Neither compares the user to the tenant.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (User at src/Admin.java:4 has no tenant field, checkRole at line 32 checks only the role, and repo.export(tenant) at line 33 uses the caller-supplied tenant), but src/Admin.java is the only file in the directory, so tenant scoping in Repo, the web layer or role assignment cannot be ruled in or out.
